input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs Product-by-Product and country-by-country until the Secondary Royalty Terms expire (13.1), a multi-year committed term, yet Ono's only at-will exit (13.2) does not arise until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, and the notice figure is redacted. Ono therefore has no convenience exit for the entire development and pre-launch period and the notice cannot be verified against the 30-day preferred or 60-90 day fallback thresholds, which is walk-away territory under T4C. Our single edit to 13.2 removes the gating trigger, fixes notice at thirty (30) days and adds a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for the post-termination period, while retaining the rationale formality verbatim and leaving 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 untouched. The fourth preferred element is already met by the existing architecture: Array's only exits are material breach (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2), none of which is a convenience right, so no confirming sentence is needed. Noted but not flagged: the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail attaches a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term, and Section 6.1 makes the upfront licence fee non-refundable; the refund wording is limited to period-allocated prepayments so it does not contradict 6.1.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: 13.3 Termination for Material Breach. Either Party may terminate this Agreement in its entirety in the event the other Party shall have materially breached or defaulted in the performance of any of its material obligations hereunder

proposal.summary: Make Ono's at-will termination right available from the Effective Date on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for the post-termination period.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our convenience exit should not be blocked until a redacted date after First Commercial Sale of both Products, so we have made the right available at any time, fixed the notice at thirty (30) days and added a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for the post-termination period; we can discuss 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.newText: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reasons by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination, and Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination.
